/help.name: Show this command reference
/help.desc: Lists the usage and purpose of every command, i.e. this help.

/mode.name: Switch conversation mode
/mode.desc: Switches how the AI answers; there are three modes now — use /task when you need a specific output format. Run /mode list to see them all.
/mode.detail:
Modes:
      chat (default) / contract (clause review) / agent (can call tools)
    Each mode states its role, output format, how much detail to give, reasoning steps,
    one input/output example and its tone, and they all share the same general requirements
    (say you do not know, one sentence when one sentence is enough, give the most likely
    answer before asking, never fabricate sources).
    Summarize / translate / code / creative writing no longer take up a mode slot:
    call them with /task summary, /task translate, /task code and /task creative.
    Old spellings such as /mode summary still work — they switch the mode and apply the
    matching template for you.
    /mode list shows each mode's description and temperature preset.

/file.name: Upload a file
/file.desc: Adds the file contents to the context so the model can answer from it.
/file.detail:
Supports Office (doc/docx/xls/xlsx/ppt/pptx), TXT, PDF and more.
    Encrypted Office documents are decrypted automatically on machines with WPS
    installed; otherwise a generic parser is used as a fallback.
    Long documents (estimated tokens above 50% of the context window) are
    summarized chunk by chunk first instead of being truncated, and the summary
    keeps pointers back to the original text.
    Loaded skills may declare additional file extensions (see the format list on
    the Installed page in Settings).

/summarize.name: Summarize the loaded document now
/summarize.desc:
Forces a chunked summary (summarize each chunk, then merge) of the loaded file and
       injects the summary instead of the full text — useful for very long contracts.
       Progress is shown live in the conversation.

/search.name: Toggle web search
/search.desc: When on, each question first searches the web for reference material (needs network).

/model.name: Inspect or switch models
/model.desc: Inspect or switch the local model.
/model.detail:
Usage: /model             show current model info (architecture, quantization, context, GPU…)
        /model list         list models in the models/ folder and in the config profiles
        /model model.gguf   switch to a local model (prefix matching supported)
        /model alias        switch to a model profile from config.models (applies its context/temperature)
    If the model is missing locally, the closest file in the repository is offered and
downloading only starts after you confirm (it can take a long time).

/clearcache.name: Clear the KV cache
/clearcache.desc:
Clears the inference engine's KV cache and input history. The system clears it
       automatically when mode/prompt/history change; clearing manually helps when
       diagnosing odd output.

/prompt.name: Set a custom system prompt
/prompt.desc: Overrides the current mode's default prompt to temporarily change the assistant's role (highest priority: it also overrides any /task template).

/temp.name: Adjust generation temperature
/temp.desc: Higher temperature means more varied answers, lower means more conservative.
/temp.detail:
Note: switching mode applies that mode's temperature preset (code 0.2 / translate 0.3 /
        contract 0.3 / summary 0.4 / general 0.7 / creative 0.9).
        Once set manually the manual value wins; /temp reset restores the preset.

/stop.name: Stop the current generation
/stop.desc: Interrupts the streaming reply in progress.
/stop.detail: (Equivalent to the ⏹ Stop button in the front end.)

/snippet.name: Snippets (managed by the front end)
/snippet.desc:
Manages the snippet templates that can be inserted into the input box with one click
       (stored by the front end in snippets.json).

/darkmode.name: Switch theme
/darkmode.desc: Switches between the dark and light interface theme (rendered immediately by the front end).

/status.name: Show current status
/status.desc: Shows model, mode, temperature, search state, turn count and the loaded file.

/clear.name: Clear the conversation
/clear.desc: Clears the history and the file context and starts over.

/undo.name: Undo
/undo.desc: Removes the most recent question and answer (one message each).

/save.name: Export the conversation
/save.desc: Exports the current conversation to a Markdown file (.md is appended automatically).

/about.name: About
/about.desc: Shows the version number and publisher information.

/exit.name: Quit
/exit.desc: Shows a farewell message; the front end closes the program within 10 seconds.

/task.name: Task template
/task.desc: Apply a task-oriented prompt template (summary, contract review, extraction, translation, code debugging, step-by-step reasoning). It is **layered on top of** the current mode (the mode sets the scene and tone, the template sets this task's output format, and the template wins on conflict). Use /task list to see all, /task off to clear.

/preset.name: Generation preset
/preset.desc: Switch between the light, balanced and quality generation presets (temperature, top_p, repetition penalty, reply length) without tuning individual parameters.

/compact.name: Compact context
/compact.desc: Compact the context right away: older turns become a summary (or are dropped in sliding-window mode), freeing room for new content without waiting for the automatic trigger.

/agent.name: Agent tools and permissions
/agent.desc: See which tools the agent may call and which are authorised, pre-authorise sensitive tools (web search, reading local files), or change the step limit; on/off is the same as switching to agent mode
/agent.detail:
In agent mode the model decides which tool to call and in what order until it reaches a conclusion;
    every step (which tool, which arguments, what came back) is shown in the conversation, and Esc stops it.

    Tools come in two tiers:
      ✅ safe: calculator, dates, unit conversion, lookup/summary inside uploaded files — enabled by default;
      🔒 sensitive: web search and reading arbitrary local files — these send data out or read local
         content, so they are off by default; enable them with /agent allow web_search.
    This version ships **no tool that writes files or runs commands** (least privilege).

    Common uses:
      /agent                    show the tool list and permission state
      /agent allow web_search   allow web search (written to config.json, persists)
      /agent deny web_search    revoke it
      /agent steps 5            force a conclusion after at most 5 tool calls
      /agent on                 switch to agent mode (same as /mode agent)

/mcp.name: MCP servers
/mcp.desc: Show MCP server status and the tools they expose; enabling or disabling a server takes effect immediately (no restart); connect actually starts the process and fetches its tool list
/mcp.detail:
MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets the agent use tools provided by **external processes**
    (databases, APIs, file systems, …). EchoDesk ships a stdio client: declare one
    command per server under mcp.servers in config.json.

    Security boundary: an MCP server is a process you configured and EchoDesk cannot
    control what it does, so its tools are **always treated as sensitive** and must be
    authorised with /agent allow first. Secret environment variables are **not**
    passed through by default — name them in passthrough_env if you need to.

    Common uses:
      /mcp                     show status and tools
      /mcp enable echo         enable a server (written to config.json)
      /mcp disable echo        disable it (takes effect immediately)
      /mcp connect             connect now and fetch the tool list

    Example: examples\mcp\echo_server.py (standard library only; configure it to
    verify the plumbing end to end).

guide.firstRun:
🎉 Getting started
1️⃣ Model: on the first launch, if the model is missing locally you will be asked whether to download it; you can also drop a .gguf file into the models/ folder yourself.
2️⃣ Launching: you can create an “EchoDesk” shortcut in the program folder and start the app by double-clicking it (already handled according to your earlier choice).
3️⃣ Long documents: when a long file such as a contract exceeds the context window it is summarised in chunks before answering, so nothing is truncated away.
4️⃣ Commands: type /help for the full command list; typing / opens the command picker.
5️⃣ Copying: every message has Copy / Markdown / Code buttons at the bottom right; you can also select text and press Ctrl+C.
6️⃣ Shortcuts: Ctrl+Enter to send · Esc to stop · Ctrl+L to clear · Ctrl+O to upload · Ctrl+Shift+C to copy everything · Ctrl+wheel to resize text
